key_insight: This paper introduces Sustainability Robotics as a new discipline that unifies scattered efforts in robotics and sustainability. It frames robotics not just as a tool to be made greener, but as a platform to actively drive environmental and societal sustainability.
problem_solved: The field is fragmented, with sustainability goals often treated separately from robotics research and design. This manifesto addresses the lack of a shared framework for aligning robotic innovation with real-world sustainability impact.
method: Proposes Sustainability Robotics as a new disciplinary vision rather than a single technical system.
Defines three guiding principles to orient research, design, and deployment toward sustainability.
Introduces two dimensions spanning sustainable design and robotics for sustainability to organize the field.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper provides a higher-level framework for designing robotic systems with measurable environmental and social value. It encourages researchers to move beyond performance metrics and consider lifecycle, deployment context, and long-term impact.
visual_elements: A two-axis framework diagram showing sustainable design vs. robotics for sustainability.
An icon-based illustration of the three guiding principles.
A pipeline graphic linking research, design, deployment, and sustainability outcomes.
A before/after comparison showing fragmented robotics efforts versus a unified Sustainability Robotics vision.
paper_authors: S. Song, B. Mazzolai, M. Kovač
